value.body: The National Informatics Centre (NIC) is the central government's IT organisation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). It builds and runs e-governance software, websites, data centres and networks for ministries, states and districts. Its regular technical posts are filled through occasional recruitment drives run by NIELIT.

items.label: Main entry posts
items.note: Recent drives also included Scientific Officer/Engineer posts

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Scientist-B has asked for a B.E./B.Tech or a relevant master's (such as M.Sc, MCA, M.E./M.Tech) in listed IT and electronics fields; Scientific/Technical Assistant-A has asked for an M.Sc, MS, MCA or B.E./B.Tech. A B.Sc or BCA alone has generally not been enough, so most B.Sc and BCA graduates apply after an MCA or M.Sc. Selection has been by a written test, plus an interview for Scientist-B, with an age limit set in each notice.

value.title: At a glance
items: Drives are not annual — the last two large rounds were in 2020 and 2023.
Work covers software development, hosting, networks and IT support for government departments, often from state or district units.
Many government IT project jobs are contractual and hired separately from these regular posts.
Eligibility, age limits and fields change with each notice, so the current advertisement is the rule that applies.
